cells.tense: The whole picture is here now, and you are seeing it plainly.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take one pattern you keep noticing among the people you're close to — what sets off what, with whom — and work it through to its logic on paper: if this, then that follows. Follow it to the end, even where it arrives at something you'd rather not find.
cells.core:
In the bonds that matter, you understand more than most people bother to. Nothing in how the people near you fit together is hidden from you — you can see what sets off what, who needs what from whom, where the fault lines run. Genuine understanding is what your closeness is built on, and it stays built because the picture is accurate, not because you're being careful.

The next thing this balance is free to feed: your own thinking. Take one pattern you keep noticing among those close to you and work it through to its logic — all the way, on paper, where it can't be tidied. The point isn't the diagram. It's that you can follow what you know to its end and still decide what to do with it yourself.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole picture. Follow it where it leads.
cells.verb: seeing it whole, with nothing left over
cells.place: among the people you're close to, where connection is meant to align

cells.tense: You will have worked out how it ends before it has had a chance to happen.
cells.act: catch the first spark before you point it anywhere
cells.ask: Once a day this week, when something between you and someone close is only just beginning — a mood, a question, a thing unsaid — catch that spark before you decide what it means or where it's going. Leave it unnamed.
cells.core:
You can read a person this way: what they'll need, what they're likely doing, how a conversation three moves from now will land. It works, and it has made you the one who knows. It also runs past the things it's reading — you settle how something ends while it's still starting, and people can feel they're being known before they've quite arrived.

You can't force freshness by trying harder. Catch the spark instead. When something between you and someone close is only beginning — a mood, a half-made plan, a thing neither of you has said — let it be nothing in particular for a moment. Don't analyse it, don't answer it. The not-yet is the actual subject here.
cells.sheetLine: Don't decide how it ends while it is still beginning.
cells.verb: seeing it whole, with nothing left over
cells.place: among the people you're close to, where connection is meant to align

cells.tense: You once read the room closely, and you have been standing outside it since.
cells.act: name the form it will take, and only that
cells.ask: Pick one bond the understanding has gone quiet in. Name the shape of the next small contact — a call of a set length, one question asked, one hour — and only that. Fix it in a single line to yourself; nothing about feeling or outcome, just the shape.
cells.core:
You know how the people close to you fit together — or you did. That understanding is still in you, and it hasn't been getting out where they are. You watch, you see it plainly, and you don't step into the room where any of it could be said. Nothing here is failing; something has gone unspent.

Trying to feel more toward anyone isn't it, and saying any of this to them isn't either. Give the pattern one direction instead. Pick one bond it hasn't reached lately, fix the shape of the next small contact in a single line — the length, the question, the hour — and load it with nothing else. Then it has somewhere to go.
cells.sheetLine: You saw the room. Name one way back into it.
cells.verb: seeing it whole, with nothing left over

cells.tense: Something is being understood between people, and it is happening through you.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: Next time you're with someone and the conversation turns so that someone has to read it — hold what's actually there before you name it. The word before its meaning, the look before the mood. Meet the thing itself, not the version you came in with.
cells.core:
In one of your connections, a clearing of the air is under way — something someone is finally saying, or finally hearing — and when asked, you would say the two of them got there. The reading of it, though, is being done through your understanding, and you're carrying it as if you were only nearby.

Put the pen down long enough to see what's arriving. When you're with someone and something new comes into the room, let it be new before you recognise it — the word before its meaning, the look before the name. You're not asked to announce anything. Only to notice that you're the turning, and to stop leaving your own part out of the account.
cells.sheetLine: The understanding moving through this is yours as well.
cells.verb: seeing it whole, with nothing left over

attempts.check: The record does not say that any particular relationship is currently going well or badly, so any core that asserts a live difficulty in a named bond would be reaching past it; each status is written instead as a condition of one capacity — understanding complete in one area of a life, meeting people from there. A reader could reasonably say 'I do see what's happening, the trouble is elsewhere' — and each ask still stands on its own, because it asks for an act, not for a diagnosis to be accepted. The sentence that serves me most is any version of 'nothing is hidden from you' — it flatters the card and says nothing the person can use, so it is left out of all four.
